CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an elderly male presenting with left arm pain that began approximately two weeks ago. He woke at 2:00 AM with severe pain in his hand and arm. He applied ice which helped ease the symptoms. He sat on the side of the bed and held his arm down attempting to improve circulation without relief. The pain gradually eased around 4-5 AM and did not recur that night. However, this pattern repeated over several nights. Patient reports the pain starts in the hand and radiates down the entire arm. He notes weakness in his hand, particularly with gripping. He confirms a prior finger injury that does not work properly. Pain is worse at night but if it occurs at night, he typically experiences symptoms the following day as well. Patient denies neck movement or shoulder movement worsening his arm symptoms. He was previously evaluated by another physician who suspected a pinched nerve and prescribed numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin, which has helped. Since then, symptoms have not bothered him at night, though his hand remains bothersome. For the last week, his neck has not been bothering him, but his hand continues to be problematic.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Neuropathy affecting knees down to feet (VA disability, 1% disabled). History of finger injury.

MEDICATIONS
Numbing medicine, neck pill, gabapentin (dose uncertain), eliquis.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a VA. He has a lady friend who helps manage his medications.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Elderly white gentleman presenting in a wheelchair, no apparent distress. Neurologic exam: 1+ bilateral biceps, triceps, brachioradialis reflexes, all negative bilaterally. Upper and lower extremities strength and sensation per template. Musculoskeletal: Non-tender over cervical spine. Mildly restricted cervical extension. Right and left lateral rotation symmetric with mild lateral neck pain but no radicular pain. Spurling's maneuver benign.

RESULTS
Cervical x-ray 6421 reveals significant disc degeneration at C5-6, and to a lower extent C4-5 and C3-4. Significant lower cervical facet arthropathy at C6-7 and C7-T1 is difficult to visualize on current x-rays.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy with possible contribution of peripheral neuropathy.
2. Neck pain in the setting of arthritis and disc degeneration.

Plan: Suspect this is a flare of cervical radiculopathy. Will order cervical MRI. Tentatively plan for left C7-T1 epidural afterwards, with exact location pending MRI results. Patient to continue home exercise program and gabapentin twice daily. Follow-up after epidural to determine level of relief. Patient denies taking blood thinners.
